questions.question: When does a default parameter value actually get used?
options: Whenever the argument is falsy (0, "", false, null, undefined)
Only when the argument is exactly undefined (not passed at all, or explicitly passed as undefined)
Only when no arguments are passed to the function at all
Default parameters are triggered by null as well as undefined
questions.explanation: Default parameters specifically check for undefined — passing null explicitly does not trigger the default, which trips people up.

questions.question: What does `user?.address?.city` return if `user.address` is undefined?
options: undefined — optional chaining short-circuits instead of throwing when it hits a nullish value
questions.explanation: Optional chaining stops and returns undefined as soon as it encounters null/undefined in the chain, rather than throwing.

questions.question: Why does `settings.volume || 50` incorrectly return 50 when `settings.volume` is explicitly `0`?
options: || falls back to its right side for ANY falsy left-hand value, and 0 is falsy, even though it's a perfectly valid, intentional setting
This is a bug in JavaScript that has since been fixed
0 is not a valid number in JavaScript
questions.explanation: || doesn't distinguish between "no value provided" and "a legitimate falsy value provided" — both 0 and missing values trigger the fallback.

questions.question: How does `??` (nullish coalescing) differ from `||` in deciding when to use the fallback?
options: They behave identically in all cases
?? only falls back when the left side is null or undefined specifically, leaving other falsy values like 0 or "" untouched
?? falls back for any falsy value, same as ||
questions.explanation: ?? was introduced specifically to fix the || problem — it narrows the fallback trigger to only null/undefined, preserving intentional falsy values.
